goals: Make Block Geometry Extensions geometries participate in Continuity connected-texture behavior when their canonical source or material-family semantics call for connection.
Preserve source-material identity and support applicable BGE-owned geometries consistently without duplicating BGE's canonical geometry ownership, material-family registry, or source-block mappings.
scope: Provide one centralized Fabric block-appearance bridge for Continuity rule selection without generating material- or geometry-specific CTM rules.
Consume BGE's typed runtime binding, canonical parent, and exact effective slab source as the sole geometry-to-material authority rather than inferring families from registry identifiers.

Project only explicitly equivalent canonical material state, including world-contextual vanilla snowy semantics for every canonical parent that actually carries SNOWY, while keeping geometry form, orientation, waterlogging, and unknown properties out of the canonical appearance.

Treat Continuity and the active resource pack as the sole material-rule authority, then veto only otherwise-positive regular or Standard Overlay decisions through one material-agnostic surface descriptor using face normal, exact world plane, rendered receiver-quad bounds, deterministic supported-geometry bounds, and real boundary contact.

Support proven cross-geometry contact among full blocks, exact ordinary slabs, Layers, and Vertical Slabs while leaving Steps, Corners, Quarter Columns, unknown topology, risky visual profiles, and unrelated Continuity behavior unchanged.

exclusions: Continuity remains the target CTM implementation; this project does not replace Continuity or implement a general CTM engine.

BGE retains ownership of geometry registration, geometry ownership, material-family relationships, and source-block mappings; this project must consume those canonical relationships rather than duplicate them or infer them from registry names.
Nibaru retains ownership of its material definitions and semantics.
This project does not modify BGE, Matcha, or unrelated resource-pack artwork during initialization.

Translucent Glass × BGE Compatibility remains a separate project responsible for translucent-glass and rendering compatibility issues that are not general CTM connectivity; this project does not absorb that scope.

Canary 5 decorates the exact Continuity 3.0.1+26.2 regular connection predicate, processor-slice, and quad seams, and redirects only StandardOverlayQuadProcessor's source-full-collision gate before retaining Continuity's native canonical semantic checks and final real-contact veto; required mixins and the controlled input hash fail closed on an incompatible implementation.
The appearance and block-state method descriptors are compiled and controlled against Minecraft Java 26.2.
Fabric runtime loader and required Mixin host declared by Canary 5.
Provides the Fabric block appearance, renderer quad, and controlled GameTest APIs used by Canary 5; 0.156.0+26.2 is the exact validation baseline.
Owns the Vertical Slab and Step base classes used by the centralized appearance and geometry policy; 2.0.7+26.2 is the exact controlled baseline.

state.milestone: Canary 5 supersedes exact Canary 4 `0.4.0-canary4` (`2406c186314aad429a610e3083e193da762a4d0da0f688b8d7dc820e8cd42b8d`). Owner runtime evidence for exact C4 is recorded without an aggregate verdict: ordinary slab regular CTM still did not visually connect; the tested podzol was one `more_slabs_stairs_and_walls:podzol_slab[type=double,waterlogged=false]`, recognized as ORDINARY_SLAB, but its appearance was its own slab with UNMAPPABLE_CANONICAL_STATE; full podzol reached successful native FINAL_OVERLAY semantics, while the double podzol slab reached CONNECT_BLOCKS_REJECT because Continuity saw the slab appearance; `nativeFull=true`, so this was not the partial-source collision gate. C4's global 200-record cap was exhausted almost entirely by approximately 198 OVERLAY records, leaving only one APPEARANCE and no REGULAR records; C4 also returned on upstream regular rejection before logging it. C5 makes canonical SNOWY projection depend on the canonical state's actual property, adds category-bounded diagnostics and a narrow exact Continuity processor-slice rule-selection record, and retains C4 managed partial-source promotion. Minecraft-client visual behavior remains untested.
